title: JSDoc
lede: JSDoc here is a real typing surface, not decoration: the type body of a tag is parsed by the same type parser an inline annotation uses, so a comment can supply a type where nothing else does. The recurring divergence is deliberate erasure — the class/access tags (@readonly, @private, @override, @satisfies, @enum, @implements) are accepted and stripped without enforcement, matching how this compiler already erases the inline TS keywords they mirror; enforcing only the doc-comment spelling would be backwards. @param/@returns/@typedef/@template do the load-bearing work but never override an inline type, and two legacy function-as-constructor tags (@import, @constructor) are out of scope in favor of real class declarations.

entries.name: @type
entries.description: Annotates a variable, class field, or type-alias position. The value string runs through the real type parser, so the whole type-expression grammar below is available inside it — including this compiler's integer width keywords.
entries.snippet:
/** @type {uint8} */
let r = 255
r = r + 1
console.log(r)                    // 0  (wrapped at 8 bits)
differences: Applies to variable, class-field, and type-alias positions

entries.name: @param (aliases @arg, @argument)
entries.description: Types a parameter from the doc comment — the core of the typed-JavaScript workflow. It fills in only where the parameter has no inline annotation, so an existing `: T` always wins. The type body uses the full grammar below, and a `{number=}` or `[name]` optional decoration is recognized and stripped.
differences: Fills only a parameter with no inline `: T` annotation and no destructuring pattern (an inline type wins)
A `{...T}` varargs type is stripped to its base `T`; binding it to a body that reads `arguments` still needs the unsupported `arguments` object — use a declared `...rest: T[]` parameter

entries.name: @returns (alias @return)
entries.description: Supplies a function's return type from the doc comment, filling in only when there is no inline `: RetType`.
differences: Fills only when the function has no inline `: RetType`

entries.name: @typedef
entries.description: Declares a named type. Both spellings work — the `@typedef {Object} Name` + `@property {T} field` form and the inline `@typedef {{x: number}} Name` object literal — and the result is synthesized into a `type Name = …` declaration, so it resolves anywhere a type name does.
differences: Both forms work: `@typedef {Object} Name` + `@property {T} field`, and the inline `@typedef {{x: number}} Name` object literal
A `@typedef {T} Name` alias to a **width keyword** (`int32`) does not propagate the integer semantics — the same pre-existing limit a TS `type X = int32` alias has

entries.name: @callback
entries.description: Declares a named function type from its `@param`/`@returns` tags, synthesized into a function-type alias that is usable wherever a type name is.
differences: Param/return types use the full type-expression grammar

entries.name: @template
entries.description: The JSDoc form of a `<T>` generic — it sets the function's type-parameter list and drives the exact same monomorphization a TS `<T>` does. `@erased` is the compile-once variant.
differences: Inherits the TS generics scope: V1 monomorphization needs an inferable `T`/`T[]`-typed parameter, no explicit call-site type arguments; a `{Base}` constraint on a multi-name tag applies to the first name (matching TS)

entries.name: @satisfies
entries.description: Accepted and erased, parity with the erased TS `satisfies` operator — the value keeps its own type and gets no conformance check.
differences: Accepted and erased — the value keeps its own type, no `satisfies`-style excess-property/conformance check (parity with the erased TS `satisfies` operator)

entries.name: @enum
entries.description: Tags a `const` object for value access (`Dir.Up`). It stays a plain object, not a nominal enum type.
differences: The tagged `const` object works for value access (`Dir.Up`); it is a plain object, not a nominal enum type — no reverse mapping, no enum-member type narrowing

entries.name: @this
entries.description: Accepted and erased. A `this` parameter type is not separately modeled — `this` is bound by the class method it lives in.
differences: Accepted and erased; a `this` parameter type is not separately modeled (`this` is bound by the class method it lives in)

entries.name: @extends (alias @augments)
entries.description: Accepted and erased — the class's own `extends` clause does the work; the tag does not add type arguments to a generic base.
differences: Accepted and erased — the class's own `extends` clause does the work; the tag does not add type arguments to a generic base

entries.name: @implements
entries.description: Accepted and erased — like a TS `implements` clause here, it does not strictly enforce structural conformance.
differences: Accepted and erased — like a TS `implements` clause here, it does not strictly enforce structural conformance

entries.name: @public
entries.description: Accepted and erased, not enforced — the same stance as the TS `public` field modifier here.
differences: Accepted and erased, not enforced — the same stance as the TS `public` field modifier here

entries.name: @private
entries.description: Accepted and erased, not enforced — no access checking (the TS `private` modifier is likewise erased, not enforced, here).
differences: Accepted and erased, not enforced — no access checking (the TS `private` modifier is likewise erased, not enforced, here)

entries.name: @protected
entries.description: Accepted and erased, not enforced.
differences: Accepted and erased, not enforced

entries.name: @readonly
entries.description: Accepted and erased, not enforced — no mutation checking, parity with the erased TS `readonly` modifier.
differences: Accepted and erased, not enforced — no mutation checking (parity with the erased TS `readonly` modifier)

entries.name: @override
entries.description: Accepted and erased — no override-consistency check.
differences: Accepted and erased — no override-consistency check

entries.name: @deprecated
entries.description: Documentation-only; accepted with no compile effect, parity with TS's runtime behavior.
differences: Documentation-only; accepted with no compile effect, but there is no tooling layer to surface a deprecation warning

entries.name: @see
entries.description: Documentation-only, no type effect — accepted, parity with TS.

entries.name: @link
entries.description: Documentation-only, no type effect — accepted, parity with TS.

entries.name: @author
entries.description: Documentation-only, no type effect — accepted, parity with TS.

entries.name: @import
entries.description: The comment-form import statement is not synthesized. Use a normal `import` plus an `import("./m").T` type reference, which does resolve — see the type-expression table.
differences: The comment-form import statement is not synthesized; use a normal `import` plus an `import("./m").T` type reference (which resolves — see the type-expression table)

entries.name: @constructor (alias @class)
entries.description: Marks a plain function as a constructor (legacy pre-`class` JS). Unsupported by design — this compiler uses real `class` declarations, not function-as-constructor.
differences: Marks a plain function as a constructor (legacy pre-`class` JS) — unsupported; this compiler uses real `class` declarations, not function-as-constructor

entries.name: Bare primitive (string, number, boolean, …)
entries.description: Resolved by the same type resolver a TS annotation uses.

entries.name: T[] array
entries.description: The `[]` suffix is handled by the resolver.

entries.name: Optional param (T=, [name])
entries.description: The optional decoration is recognized at the `@param` name/type level and stripped.
differences: Recognized at the `@param` name/type level and stripped; the parameter is not yet marked structurally optional beyond an inline `?`

entries.name: Varargs/rest (...T)
entries.description: Stripped to the base `T`; the varargs value flows into a declared `...rest` parameter.
differences: Stripped to the base `T`; the varargs body needs a declared `...rest` parameter (no `arguments`)

entries.name: Union (A | B)
entries.description: The JSDoc string is parsed by the real type parser, so a union resolves like an inline one.
differences: Inherits the union V1 scope (scalar/object/`ReadableStream` members, narrowing rules — see the Type system page)

entries.name: Nullable (?T)
entries.description: A leading `?` marker becomes a union with null (`?number` → `number | null`).
differences: The leading marker (`?number` → `number | null`); a `?` buried mid-expression is left to the parser

entries.name: Non-null (!T)
entries.description: The marker is stripped (`!number` → `number`) — TS treats non-null as no semantic change.
differences: The marker is stripped (`!number` → `number`) — TS treats non-null as no semantic change

entries.name: Object shape ({ a: string, b: number })
entries.statusRow: Object shape ({ a: string, b: number })
entries.description: Inline object shapes resolve, and nested braces are supported (`@param {{x: number}}`) via balanced-brace scanning.
differences: Nested braces are supported (`@param {{x: number}}`) via balanced-brace scanning

entries.name: Array.<T> / Array<T> (generic array form)
entries.description: The Closure dot form (`Array.<T>`) is normalized to `Array<T>`.

entries.name: Object.<K, V> (index map)
entries.description: Normalized to `Record<K, V>`, but per-key field/index access on a `Record` isn't supported, so it compiles only where a `Record` would.
differences: Normalized to `Record<K, V>`, but per-key field/index access on a `Record` isn't supported (index signatures are a separate ❌), so it compiles only where a `Record` would

entries.name: Function type (function(A): B)
entries.description: Rewritten to the arrow form `(arg0: A) => B`.
differences: Rewritten to the arrow form `(arg0: A) => B`; a nested `function(...)` inside another type is not rewritten (rare)

entries.name: * / ? (Closure any/unknown)
entries.description: Both are normalized to `any`.

entries.name: import("./m").T type
entries.description: The `import("./m").Name` qualifier is dropped to the bare `Name`, which resolves under whole-program compilation when that module is part of the build.
differences: The `import("./m").Name` qualifier is dropped to the bare `Name`, which resolves under whole-program compilation when that module is part of the build (typically because the file also imports from it) — a `Name` not otherwise pulled in won't resolve; the `typeof import(...)` value form is out of scope

entries.name: @typedef/@callback-defined names
entries.description: Names introduced by `@typedef`/`@callback` resolve wherever a type name does; inline `{{…}}` typedefs work too.

entries.name: Legacy synonyms (String→string, …)
entries.description: The capitalized Closure-era synonyms remap to their lowercase primitives.
differences: `String`/`Number`/`Boolean`/`Void`/`Undefined`/`Null` remap to the lowercase primitive; bare `Object`/`object` are left as-is

entries.name: Integer width keywords (@type {int8..int64, uint8..uint64})
entries.description: A compiler extension with no TypeScript equivalent: the real-integer escape hatch — exact semantics and bit-width storage, also usable in `@param`/`@returns`.

entries.name: Extended float keywords (@type {float32, float64})
entries.description: A compiler extension with no TypeScript equivalent: `float64` is the default `number`; `float32` is a narrower slot.

entries.name: @erased (generic single-body compilation)
entries.description: A compiler extension with no TypeScript equivalent: opts a generic function out of monomorphization — the JSDoc analogue of a `<T>` the compiler compiles once.
